description:
Hi! I'm Sadaf, a software engineering student who enjoys full-stack development and system design. We're taking on "Abandoned but not Forgotten": telling the stories of NASA's discarded equipment on the Moon and Mars through an interactive web experience.

Looking for: a UI/UX designer, a researcher to dig into NASA mission data, and a writer for short narratives. Beginners welcome! Join us and let's build something memorable.
summary: Abandoned but Not Forgotten is a free, mobile-friendly website where five NASA machines left on the Moon, on Mars and in deep space tell their own stories in the first person: Apollo 11's Eagle lunar module, Viking 1, Spirit, Voyager 1 and Ingenuity. Built for kids aged 10–14, each story card has four chapters: My story, How I worked (a step-by-step mission timeline), What I found, and Where I am now. Each card also has key dates, a "Did you know?" fact and official NASA images with credits. A 5-question quiz with instant feedback and a score closes the experience. Every fact was checked against NASA sources (science.nasa.gov, NSSDCA and the NASA Image and Video Library). Abandoned hardware is often seen as space junk. Our project shows these machines as explorers with missions, struggles and discoveries, so young learners remember how space exploration works, not just a list of dates.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Abandoned but Not Forgotten is an interactive storytelling website about NASA hardware left on the Moon, on Mars and in deep space. Five machines speak in the first person: Apollo 11's Eagle lunar module, Viking 1, Spirit, Voyager 1 and Ingenuity. Each story card includes:

- A first-person introduction (e.g. "I'm Spirit! I was built to explore Mars for 90 days. I kept going for over six years.")

- Two official NASA images with captions and credits

- Four chapter tabs: My story, How I worked (a numbered timeline showing how the machine actually operated), What I found, and Where I am now (key dates and current status)

- A "Did you know?" fact

Visitors can filter machines by location (Moon, Mars, Deep space). A 5-question quiz gives instant feedback, an explanation for every answer, and a final score. A Sources section links to every NASA page used.

HOW IT WORKS

The site is static: HTML, CSS and plain JavaScript, with no frameworks, no backend and no login. All content lives in one file (data.js), so a teacher or student can correct a fact or add a new machine without touching the code. app.js reads that data and builds the cards, tabs, filters, quiz and source list. It is hosted free on GitHub Pages.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

Instead of listing facts, the project shows HOW each mission worked and what it struggled with: Spirit dragging a broken wheel and uncovering nearly pure silica, a sign of a wetter ancient Mars; Viking 1 silenced by one faulty command from Earth; Ingenuity flying 72 times when up to 5 test flights were planned. Storytelling makes the science personal and memorable for kids aged 10–14. The timing is special: Voyager 1 is expected to reach one light-day from Earth on 18 November 2026.

ACCURACY

Every fact was checked against science.nasa.gov, NSSDCA and NASA Image and Video Library descriptions. Where NASA sources were unclear (for example, the exact number of Voyager 1 instruments still on), the site uses careful wording instead of guessing.

ACCESSIBILITY AND DESIGN

Mobile-first layout, large fonts, high-contrast colours, alt text on every image, keyboard focus outlines, a skip link, and screen-reader announcements for quiz feedback.

TOOLS

HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, GitHub, GitHub Pages, Visual Studio Code, Google Slides (demo), Claude by Anthropic (AI-assisted code and draft text).

Source code: https://github.com/sadaf-saleem/forgotten-frontier

AI DISCLOSURE

The code and draft text were generated with AI assistance (Claude, by Anthropic). Sadaf Saleem directed the project, chose the machines and storytelling format, reviewed all content, and checked the facts against NASA sources. No AI-generated images were used; all images are official NASA images with credits.
